# Reference conceptual model

**Important:** stereotype annotations in this catalog are provisional modelling commitments, not a claim of automated OntoUML validation. The DOT/SVG diagrams are visual views, not native OntoUML exchange files.

## How UFO stereotypes are represented in OWL

| Stereotype | Classes | UFO | OWL/TTL | Not expressible in OWL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| «kind» | `Artwork`, `Manifestation`, `Selection`, `AnalysisUnit`, `InterpretationRecord`, `InterpretiveJustification`, `InterpretationChallenge`, `InterpretationAssessment`, `AssessmentCriterion`, `DepictedElement`, `SituationDescription`, `SituationPattern`, `PatternCondition`, `EmpiricalCase`, `EmpiricalClaim`, `ReferenceSource`, `EvidenceItem`, `CorrespondenceClaim`, `EvidenceAssessment`, `ExplanationHypothesis`, `DerivationClaim`, `TransformationAspect` | Rigid sortal: supplies the identity principle of its instances, which cannot stop instantiating it while they exist. | Declared as `owl:Class`. | Rigidity and the identity principle are not expressible in OWL; disjointness between kinds is not declared. |
| «subkind» | `DepictedAgent`, `IntentionalStateDescription` | Rigid sortal that specializes a kind and inherits its identity principle. | `owl:Class` with `rdfs:subClassOf` the specialized class. | Rigidity is not expressible; the subclass axiom is the only commitment represented. |
| «event» | `InterpretiveAct`, `EmpiricalEvent`, `CreativeAct` | Perdurant (UFO-B): an occurrence that unfolds in time and has participants; it is not an object. | `owl:Class`; participation is represented by object properties. | Temporal extent and ordering of events are not represented in this version (no time properties). |
| «situation» | `EmpiricalSituation` | Situation (UFO-B): a configuration of entities that obtains at a point in time and may trigger or result from events. | `owl:Class`. | The time point at which the situation obtains and its constituents are not represented. |
| «relator» | `CreativeContribution` | Relator (UFO-A): an endurant existentially dependent on the entities it connects; the truthmaker of a material relation. | `owl:Class` with object properties to its relata; SHACL enforces the mediation cardinalities. | Existential dependence and the derived material relation are not expressible in OWL. |
| «roleMixin» | `Analyst`, `CreativeAgent` | Anti-rigid non-sortal: classifies entities of different kinds by a relational property (taking part in an act); supplies no identity. | `owl:Class`; individuals from external vocabularies are classified into it by an RDFS reasoner through the `rdfs:range` of the connecting relation. | Anti-rigidity (an entity may stop playing the role) is not expressible; any IRI used with the relation is classified. |
| «type» | `DerivationType`, `DerivationRegime`, `ArtisticDimension`, `TransformationOperation`, `CreativeRole` | High-order type: its instances are themselves types (kinds of derivation, dimensions, roles…). | `owl:Class` whose instances are SKOS concepts (each concept is typed both `skos:Concept` and this class). | In OWL 2 DL the concepts are individuals, not classes, so multi-level instantiation is approximated, not represented. |

## Classes

### `Artwork` — artwork

**Definition:** Identifiable artistic creation across media and manifestations.

| | |
|---|---|
| **UFO / OntoUML** | «kind» — Rigid sortal: supplies the identity principle of its instances, which cannot stop instantiating it while they exist. |
| **Grounding** | UFO-C social/information object (domain commitment) |
| **Dependency** | historically on creation; not on a single copy |
| **In OWL/TTL** | `aro:Artwork a owl:Class`; domain of: `hasManifestation`; range of: `realizesArtwork`, `hasSourceAnchor`, `hasDerivedAnchor`, `producesCreation` |
| **SHACL** | — |
| **Not expressible in OWL** | Rigidity and the identity principle are not expressible in OWL; disjointness between kinds is not declared. |
| **gUFO pattern (not imported)** | `rdf:type gufo:Kind` — As a UFO-C information object it has no specific gUFO counterpart. |
| **Package** | `artwork` |

### `Analyst` — analyst

**Definition:** Any human agent, identified in an external vocabulary, insofar as they interpret or assess. Agent identity is represented by the external vocabulary, not by ARO.

| | |
|---|---|
| **UFO / OntoUML** | «roleMixin» — Anti-rigid non-sortal: classifies entities of different kinds by a relational property (taking part in an act); supplies no identity. |
| **Grounding** | UFO-A anti-rigid non-sortal (roleMixin); agents are individuals of external ontologies |
| **Dependency** | relationally on participation in an InterpretiveAct; identity supplied by external kinds |
| **In OWL/TTL** | `aro:Analyst a owl:Class`; external individuals are classified into it by an RDFS reasoner through the `rdfs:range` of the connecting relation; range of: `hasParticipant` |
| **SHACL** | — |
| **Not expressible in OWL** | Anti-rigidity (an entity may stop playing the role) is not expressible; any IRI used with the relation is classified. |
| **gUFO pattern (not imported)** | `rdf:type gufo:RoleMixin` |
| **Alignments** | `rdfs:seeAlso` `prov:Agent`, `rdfs:seeAlso` `foaf:Person`, `rdfs:seeAlso` `schema:Person` |
| **Package** | `interpretation` |

### `DerivationClaim` — derivation claim

**Definition:** Contestable assertion, made by an agent, that one artistic entity (artwork, manifestation or selection) derives from another in specified ways. The derived entity is represented as a creation in its own right; legality and originality are outside the scope of the ontology.

| | |
|---|---|
| **UFO / OntoUML** | «kind» — Rigid sortal: supplies the identity principle of its instances, which cannot stop instantiating it while they exist. |
| **Grounding** | UFO-C information object; not a UFO relator nor an asserted fact |
| **Dependency** | exactly one source anchor and one derived anchor; typed by at least one derivation type |
| **In OWL/TTL** | `aro:DerivationClaim a owl:Class`; domain of: `hasSourceAnchor`, `hasDerivedAnchor`, `hasDerivationType`, `hasRegime`, `hasTransformation`, `derivationJustifiedBy`, `derivationRealizedBy`, `claimProducedByAct`, `derivationReferencesSource`, `derivationExtent`; range of: `assessesDerivation` |
| **SHACL** | `hasSourceAnchor` (min 1, max 1); `hasDerivedAnchor` (min 1, max 1); `hasDerivationType` (min 1, class `DerivationType`); `hasRegime` (class `DerivationRegime`); SPARQL: Derivation anchors must be an Artwork, Manifestation or Selection.; SPARQL: Source and derived anchors must differ. |
| **Not expressible in OWL** | Rigidity and the identity principle are not expressible in OWL; disjointness between kinds is not declared. |
| **gUFO pattern (not imported)** | `rdf:type gufo:Kind` — As a UFO-C information object it has no specific gUFO counterpart. |
| **Alignments** | `rdfs:seeAlso` `prov:wasDerivedFrom`, `rdfs:seeAlso` `schema:isBasedOn`, `rdfs:seeAlso` `wdt:P144` |
| **Package** | `derivation` |

        "Estereótipo OntoUML (provisório): kind; fundamentação: objeto informacional UFO-C; nem relator UFO nem fato afirmado; dependência: exatamente uma âncora de origem e uma derivada; tipificada por ao menos um tipo de derivação"@pt-BR ;

### `CreativeAgent` — creative agent

**Definition:** Any agent, identified and described in an external vocabulary (PROV-O, FOAF, schema.org, Wikidata...), insofar as it contributes to a creative act. Agent identity is represented by the external vocabulary, not by ARO.

| | |
|---|---|
| **UFO / OntoUML** | «roleMixin» — Anti-rigid non-sortal: classifies entities of different kinds by a relational property (taking part in an act); supplies no identity. |
| **Grounding** | UFO-A anti-rigid non-sortal (roleMixin); agents are individuals of external ontologies |
| **Dependency** | relationally on a CreativeContribution; identity supplied by external kinds |
| **In OWL/TTL** | `aro:CreativeAgent a owl:Class`; external individuals are classified into it by an RDFS reasoner through the `rdfs:range` of the connecting relation; range of: `contributionBy` |
| **SHACL** | — |
| **Not expressible in OWL** | Anti-rigidity (an entity may stop playing the role) is not expressible; any IRI used with the relation is classified. |
| **gUFO pattern (not imported)** | `rdf:type gufo:RoleMixin` |
| **Alignments** | `rdfs:seeAlso` `prov:Agent`, `rdfs:seeAlso` `foaf:Agent`, `rdfs:seeAlso` `schema:Person`, `rdfs:seeAlso` `schema:Organization` |
| **Package** | `derivation` |

### `CreativeContribution` — creative contribution

**Definition:** Participation of one creative agent in one creative act under one or more roles.

| | |
|---|---|
| **UFO / OntoUML** | «relator» — Relator (UFO-A): an endurant existentially dependent on the entities it connects; the truthmaker of a material relation. |
| **Grounding** | UFO-A relator; role qualification via CreativeRole |
| **Dependency** | existentially on the act and the agent |
| **In OWL/TTL** | `aro:CreativeContribution a owl:Class`; relata linked by object properties; mediation cardinalities enforced by SHACL; domain of: `contributionBy`, `contributionRole`; range of: `hasContribution` |
| **SHACL** | `contributionBy` (min 1, max 1, IRI); `contributionRole` (min 1, class `CreativeRole`) |
| **Not expressible in OWL** | Existential dependence and the derived material relation are not expressible in OWL. |
| **gUFO pattern (not imported)** | `rdf:type gufo:Kind` + `rdfs:subClassOf gufo:Relator` (relata via `gufo:mediates`) |
| **Package** | `derivation` |

## Datatype properties

| Property | Label | Domain | Datatype | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `identifier` | identifier | — | `string` | Local identifier of a record; a stable URI is recommended. Not identity in the world. |
| `textValue` | text value | — | `rdf:langString` | Human-readable text (labels, descriptions, explanations). Use language-tagged literals; the same resource may carry one value per language. |
| `selectorExpression` | selector expression | `Selection` | `string` | Compact selector shortcut; prefer hasSelector with W3C Web Annotation selectors. |
| `sourceURL` | source URL | `ReferenceSource` | `anyURI` | Web address of a reference source (news page, article, dataset, video...). Availability is not guaranteed and a link is not a credibility claim. |
| `externalLink` | external link | — | `anyURI` | Web address where the represented entity can be consulted: an artwork page, a recording, the exact location of an evidence item, a case report. Usable on any resource; a link is not a credibility claim. |
| `issuedDate` | issued date | — | `date` | Publication date when known. |
| `retrievedAt` | retrieved at | — | `dateTime` | Capture provenance timestamp. |
| `confidenceScore` | confidence score | — | `decimal` | Application-defined confidence in [0,1]; not a calibrated probability. |
| `isRequiredCondition` | is required condition | `PatternCondition` | `boolean` | Whether a pattern condition is mandatory (true) or contextual (false). |
| `languageTag` | language tag | — | `string` | BCP 47 tag of the main language of a resource, e.g. en, pt-BR, es. |
| `versionLabel` | version label | — | `string` | Application version label. |
| `derivationExtent` | derivation extent | `DerivationClaim` | `rdf:langString` | Free-text extent of reuse (e.g. "4-second loop", "whole plot"); language-tagged. |

## Controlled vocabularies (SKOS)

### `DerivationTypeScheme` — Derivation types

Non-exclusive kinds of derivation grouped in five families; one claim may carry several types. Grounded in Genette, Tillett/Smiraglia, Burkholder, Rajewsky, Hutcheon and Jenkins (see derivation-typology.md).

| Concept | Label | Broader | Definition | Literature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Rerealization` | re-realization | — | New realization of substantially the same content; bibliographically often a new expression of the same work. | Tillett 1991; Smiraglia 2001; IFLA LRMoo 2024 |
| `Translation` | translation | `Rerealization` | Rendering of verbal content in another language. Genette also classes it as a serious transformation (transposition). | Smiraglia 2001; Genette 1982 |
| `Performance` | performance | `Rerealization` | New performance of an existing work (recital, staging, recording). | Smiraglia 2001 |
| `CoverVersion` | cover version | `Performance` | Popular-music performance or recording of an existing song by other performers; the term is systematically ambiguous, so record dimensions too. The covering artist is a creator in their own right. | Mosser 2008; Mag Uidhir, Magnus & Magnus 2013 |
| `Arrangement` | arrangement | `Rerealization` | Reworking of instrumentation, harmony or form while keeping the piece recognizable. | Burkholder 1994 |
| `Transcription` | transcription | `Rerealization` | Transfer to another notation or instrument. | Burkholder 1994 |
| `Revision` | revision | `Rerealization` | Successive version by the same or authorized agents (revised edition, director's cut, remaster). | Smiraglia 2001 (successive derivations) |
| `Abridgment` | abridgment / extraction | `Rerealization` | Derivation keeping a reduced part of the source (abridgment, excerpt, radio edit). | Smiraglia 2001 (extractions) |
| `Amplification` | amplification | `Rerealization` | Source reproduced with added material (annotated or illustrated edition, commentary track). | Smiraglia 2001 (amplifications) |
| `Remake` | remake | `Rerealization` | New audiovisual production based on an earlier production of the same story. | Verevis 2006 |
| `ExtendedRemix` | extended remix | `Rerealization` | Longer or re-edited version of the same recording that keeps its identity (e.g. club or extended mix). | Navas 2012 (extended remix) |
| `Incorporation` | incorporation / copresence | — | Material of, or explicit reference to, the source is present within a new whole. | Genette 1982 (intertextuality); Burkholder 1994 |
| `Quotation` | quotation | `Incorporation` | Explicit, recognizable reproduction of an excerpt, verbal, musical or visual. | Genette 1982; Burkholder 1994 |
| `Allusion` | allusion | `Incorporation` | Indirect reference whose full sense presupposes recognition of the source. | Genette 1982 |
| `UnacknowledgedBorrowing` | unacknowledged borrowing | `Incorporation` | Literal borrowing presented without acknowledgment of the source (Genette's 'plagiat'); a descriptive textual relation, not a legal or moral judgment. | Genette 1982 |
| `Sampling` | sampling | `Incorporation` | Reuse of a portion of an existing recording. | Schloss 2004; Navas 2012 |
| `Interpolation` | interpolation | `Incorporation` | Re-performance of a portion of the source inside a new work, without reusing the recording. | Schloss 2004 |
| `Paraphrase` | paraphrase | `Incorporation` | Source material reworked into a new line or passage while remaining traceable. | Burkholder 1994 |
| `Medley` | medley | `Incorporation` | Succession of several existing pieces or excerpts. | Burkholder 1994 |
| `Collage` | collage / mashup | `Incorporation` | Juxtaposition of several sources in one new whole. | Burkholder 1994; Navas 2012 |
| `Remix` | remix | `Incorporation` | Selective or reflexive recombination of an existing recording's elements into a new whole; the remixer is a creator in their own right. | Navas 2012 (selective and reflexive remix) |
| `Appropriation` | appropriation | `Incorporation` | Re-presentation of an existing work or image, often whole, in a new context that changes its sense. | Navas 2012 |
| `Ekphrasis` | ekphrasis | `Incorporation` | Representation in one medium of a work from another medium (e.g. poem about a painting); an intermedial reference. | Rajewsky 2005 (intermedial reference) |
| `Transformation` | transformation | — | Hypertextual derivation that changes content, form or context of the source. | Genette 1982 (hypertextuality) |
| `Adaptation` | adaptation | `Transformation` | Acknowledged, extended transposition of a work for another form, audience or context (Genette's serious transformation). | Hutcheon 2006; Genette 1982 |
| `IntermedialAdaptation` | intermedial adaptation | `Adaptation` | Adaptation across media (novel to film, film to game, song to music video, novelization). | Rajewsky 2005 (medial transposition); Hutcheon 2006 |
| `Parody` | parody | `Transformation` | Transformation of a source in a playful or critical regime; repetition with critical difference. | Genette 1982; Hutcheon 1985 |
| `Travesty` | travesty | `Transformation` | Satirical transformation that keeps the content but degrades its style or register. | Genette 1982 |
| `Variation` | variation | `Transformation` | Successive transformations of a given theme or motif. | Burkholder 1994 |
| `Imitation` | imitation | — | Derivation through imitating the manner or style of the source rather than reworking its content. | Genette 1982 (hypertextuality) |
| `Pastiche` | pastiche | `Imitation` | Imitation of a style in a playful or affectionate regime. | Genette 1982; Dyer 2007 |
| `Caricature` | caricature (charge) | `Imitation` | Imitation of a style in a satirical regime. | Genette 1982 |
| `SeriousImitation` | serious imitation (forgerie) | `Imitation` | Imitation aiming to be taken as in the manner of the source, e.g. apocryphal continuation; not necessarily fraud. | Genette 1982 |
| `Extension` | extension | — | New work extending the fictional world, timeline or cast of the source. | Tillett 1991 (sequential); Jenkins 1992 |
| `Continuation` | continuation | `Extension` | Work continuing the story of the source. | Tillett 1991 |
| `Sequel` | sequel | `Continuation` | Continuation set after the source. | Tillett 1991 |
| `Prequel` | prequel | `Continuation` | Continuation set before the source. | Tillett 1991 |
| `SpinOff` | spin-off | `Extension` | Work centred on secondary elements (characters, places) of the source. | Jenkins 1992 |
| `Crossover` | crossover | `Extension` | Work combining characters or worlds from two or more sources. | Jenkins 1992 |
| `FanWork` | fan work | `Extension` | Non-official derivation by audience members; also type the mechanism (parody, continuation, crossover...). | Jenkins 1992 |

## Controlled vocabularies (SKOS)

### `ArtisticDimensionScheme` — Artistic dimensions

Dimensions for annotation, grouped by medium family (narrative, verbal, music, visual, audiovisual, cross-media, paratext).

| Concept | Label | Broader | Definition | Literature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NarrativeDimension` | narrative | — | Story-level and discourse-level properties of narratives in any medium. | Chatman 1978; Genette 1972 |
| `PlotDimension` | plot | `NarrativeDimension` | Sequence of represented events. | Chatman 1978 |
| `CharacterDimension` | character | `NarrativeDimension` | Represented agents and their traits. | Chatman 1978 |
| `SettingDimension` | setting | `NarrativeDimension` | Represented time and place. | Chatman 1978 |
| `SituationDimension` | represented situation | `NarrativeDimension` | Represented situations, comparable through SituationPattern. | — |
| `NarrationDimension` | narration / voice | `NarrativeDimension` | Who narrates and from which narrative level. | Genette 1972 |
| `FocalizationDimension` | focalization / point of view | `NarrativeDimension` | Whose perception or knowledge filters the story. | Genette 1972 |
| `NarrativeTimeDimension` | narrative time | `NarrativeDimension` | Order, duration and frequency of events in the telling. | Genette 1972 |
| `TextDimension` | verbal text | — | Verbal content in any medium. | — |
| `LyricsDimension` | lyrics | `TextDimension` | Sung or spoken verbal text of a song. | — |
| `DialogueDimension` | dialogue | `TextDimension` | Speech attributed to characters. | — |
| `DictionDimension` | diction / register | `TextDimension` | Vocabulary, register and verbal style. | Genette 1982 |
| `VersificationDimension` | versification | `TextDimension` | Metre, rhyme and stanza form. | — |
| `LanguageDimension` | language | `TextDimension` | Natural language of verbal content. | — |
| `MusicDimension` | music and sound | — | Musical and sonic parameters. | Burkholder 1994 |
| `MelodyDimension` | melody | `MusicDimension` | Pitch–rhythm contour of a musical line. | — |
| `HarmonyDimension` | harmony | `MusicDimension` | Chordal and tonal organization. | — |

## Controlled vocabularies (SKOS)

### `DerivationRegimeScheme` — Derivation regimes

Stance of a derivation toward its source, orthogonal to its type (after Genette's regimes).

| Concept | Label | Broader | Definition | Literature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PlayfulRegime` | playful | — | Derivation aimed at play or amusement. | Genette 1982 |
| `SatiricalRegime` | satirical / critical | — | Derivation aimed at mocking or criticizing the source or its world. | Genette 1982; Hutcheon 1985 |
| `SeriousRegime` | serious | — | Derivation without comic or critical aim. | Genette 1982 |
| `ReverentialRegime` | reverential / homage | — | Derivation explicitly honouring the source (ARO addition, not in Genette). | ARO |

## Controlled vocabularies (SKOS)

### `TransformationOperationScheme` — Transformation operations

What a derivation does to one artistic dimension.

| Concept | Label | Broader | Definition | Literature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Retained` | retained | — | Dimension kept substantially as in the source. | — |
| `Modified` | modified | — | Dimension present in both but changed. | — |
| `Added` | added | — | Dimension content absent from the source. | — |
| `Removed` | removed | — | Source content omitted in the derivation. | — |
| `Recontextualized` | recontextualized | — | Content kept but placed in a different context that changes its sense. | — |

## Controlled vocabularies (SKOS)

### `CreativeRoleScheme` — Creative roles

Roles qualifying a creative contribution; extensible.

| Concept | Label | Broader | Definition | Literature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AuthorRole` | author | — | Originator of verbal or narrative content. | — |
| `ComposerRole` | composer | — | Originator of musical content. | — |
| `LyricistRole` | lyricist | — | Author of lyrics. | — |
| `PerformerRole` | performer | — | Agent performing a manifestation. | — |
| `ArrangerRole` | arranger | — | Agent producing an arrangement. | — |
| `TranslatorRole` | translator | — | Agent producing a translation. | — |
| `AdapterRole` | adapter | — | Agent producing an adaptation (e.g. screenwriter). | — |
| `ProducerRole` | producer | — | Agent responsible for producing a recording or production. | — |
| `DirectorRole` | director | — | Agent directing an audiovisual or stage work. | — |
| `RemixerRole` | remixer | — | Agent producing a remix or sample-based work. | — |
